notes.optimize: Most "best settings" guides are generic and one-size-fits-all. These tweaks are the ones vetted safe AND reversible for a rig like yours — every one snapshots its prior state before it touches anything.
notes.diagnostics: Most people never see their PC's real parts list. This is the honest inventory — read straight from the machine, nothing installed.
notes.benchmark: Benchmarks are noisy: two identical runs never score identical. Compy grades changes against that noise floor, so luck can't be called a win.
notes.latency: One click crosses the mouse, USB, Windows, the GPU and your monitor before you see it land — every hop adds delay, and each one is measurable.
notes.tuning: Undervolting asks the chip to do the same work on less power — often cooler and just as fast. How far yours goes is the silicon lottery.
notes.blackbox: Windows keeps a flight recorder of every crash and freeze. Almost nobody ever reads it — this station does, in plain English.

journey.plan: 2 sessions of about 10 min: one as-is, then one with {{change}}.
journey.planGame: {{game}}: 2 sessions of about 10 min: one as-is, then one with {{change}}.
journey.oneChange: One change per run. Compy keeps it only if it measures better, and puts it back otherwise. You can use the rest of Compy while you play. If Compy closes mid-test, the change stays on until you conclude or restore it in Test.
journey.asIs: Session 1 of 2: play {{game}} as usual for about 10 minutes. Compy stops measuring when you close the game.
journey.asIsNoGame: Session 1 of 2: play your game as usual for about 10 minutes. Compy stops measuring when you close the game.
journey.withChange: Session 2 of 2: {{change}} is on. Play {{game}} the same way for about 10 minutes, then close the game.
journey.enoughMore: Play the same area for about {{secs}} s more.
journey.enoughMoreMin: Play the same area for about {{min}} min more.

journey.enough: Compy has enough; you can stop.
journey.enoughUnsettled: The frame rate in this game keeps changing, so it may not settle. You can stop now; Compy will count this session as uneven.
journey.enoughUnsettledShort: Keeps changing. Stop now; it counts as uneven.
journey.enoughUntraced: Compy can't see enough of the frame-rate trace to tell whether this session is steady. You can stop now.
journey.enoughUntracedShort: Can't check if it's steady. You can stop now.
journey.keptLow: Kept {{change}}: the frame rate in your worst moments (the 1% low) is up {{pct}}%.

putBackWhy.noChange: it made no difference Compy could measure
putBackWhy.regressed: the game ran worse with it
putBackWhy.confounded: something else changed during the test, so the result can't be trusted
putBackWhy.expired: the before-session was too old to compare against
putBackWhy.insufficientEvidence: there wasn't enough play with it on to judge
putBackWhy.notComparable: the two sessions were too different to compare fairly
putBackWhy.tooNoisy: the frame rate moved around too much to tell

journey.nextFresh: Next: {{change}}, about 20 min (a new before-session first)

retestWhy.inconclusive: {{change}} was tried before, but the frame rate moved around too much to judge. This run tries it again.
retestWhy.stale: {{change}} has a result from an older graphics driver or Windows build, so Compy can't say it still holds. This run checks it again.
retestWhy.unverified: {{change}} has a result Compy can't tie to this PC as it is now (no graphics driver or Windows build was recorded for it or for your newest session). This run records them.

journey.nothingLeft: Nothing else here is worth testing on this PC.

why.recommended: Recommended keeps a change only when the frame rate in your worst moments (the 1% low) improved beyond the normal run-to-run wobble (the noise band) and the average did not fall beyond it; otherwise the change goes back.
why.recommendedBand: Recommended keeps a change only when the frame rate in your worst moments (the 1% low) improved beyond the ±{{band}}% normal run-to-run wobble (the noise band) and the average did not fall beyond it; otherwise the change goes back.
why.maxFps: Maximum FPS keeps a change only when the average improved beyond the normal run-to-run wobble (the noise band) and the frame rate in your worst moments (the 1% low) held; otherwise the change goes back.
why.maxFpsBand: Maximum FPS keeps a change only when the average improved beyond the ±{{band}}% normal run-to-run wobble (the noise band) and the frame rate in your worst moments (the 1% low) held; otherwise the change goes back.
why.noResult: The two sessions could not be compared fairly, so nothing was judged. The line above says what got in the way, and what happened to the change.

journey.withChangeReused: {{change}} is on. Compy uses your last session as the before-reading, so this is the only session: play {{game}} the same way for about 10 minutes, then close the game.
journey.reuseRefused: Compy can't use your last session as the before-reading ({{reason}}), so it needs a new one.
journey.tooShort: That session had {{count}} readings, and Compy needs {{min}} (about 10 minutes of play). Nothing was changed.
journey.noReading: Compy didn't get a reading from that session. Nothing was changed.
journey.noReadingBehind: Compy didn't get a reading from that session: another window was in front the whole time. Nothing was changed.
journey.notStarted: Compy didn't start the test, and nothing was changed: {{reason}}
journey.restoredNoReading: The game closed before Compy had a reading, so Compy put {{change}} back the way it was. Nothing was kept.
journey.restoredBehind: Compy didn't get a reading: another window was in front the whole time, so Compy put {{change}} back the way it was. Nothing was kept.
journey.restoredError: Something went wrong, so Compy put {{change}} back the way it was. Nothing was kept. ({{reason}})
journey.restoreFailed: Something went wrong, and Compy couldn't confirm {{change}} was put back. Check it in Test → Applied & history and undo it there. ({{reason}})
journey.captureFailed: Compy couldn't start measuring. If Windows asked for permission, allow it and try again.
journey.wrongGame: That session was {{played}}, not {{planned}}, so it can't be the before-reading. Nothing was changed.
journey.interrupted: A test was interrupted: {{change}} is still on. Conclude with your latest session or put it back.
journey.interruptedOff: A test was interrupted, and Compy reads {{change}} as off now.
journey.asIsAgain: One more as-is session: play {{game}} as usual for about 10 minutes. Compy stops measuring when you close the game.
journey.unevenWhy: That session swung from {{first}} to {{second}} fps, too uneven to compare against.
journey.untracedWhy: Compy couldn't check how steady that session was, so it can't compare against it.
journey.unevenAgain: Nothing has been changed yet. Play one more as-is session of {{game}}, about 10 minutes.
journey.unevenFinal: Nothing has been changed yet. You can test {{change}} on this session anyway, or stop here.

journey.progressStale_other: {{count}} results are from an older graphics driver or Windows build.

realPlay.startAck: I understand, test it while I play normally

realPlay.collecting: Keep playing, Compy is still collecting ({{have}} of {{need}} sessions).

realPlay.noteNone: Compy didn't save a session of {{game}} that time, so nothing new was counted.

stop.putBackInHistory: {{change}} was put back in Test → Applied & history, so the test can't go on.

stop.otherChange: Another Compy change was applied or undone during the test, so later sessions can't be compared.

stop.windowOver: The {{days}} days for this test are over.
stop.beforeMissing: The sessions from before the change are no longer in Compy's session history, so there is nothing to compare against.
stop.other: This test can't go on as it is.

stoppedOn.cantTell: Compy can't tell whether {{change}} is on right now.
stoppedOn.stillOn: {{change}} is still on, but this test can't reach a result.

rule.recommended: Real play compares your sessions with the change on against your sessions without it, played however you play. Recommended keeps a change only when it is likely better: the 1% low (the worst moments) higher by more than the allowance for normal swings between sessions, and the average not lower by more. Otherwise the change goes back.
rule.maxFps: Real play compares your sessions with the change on against your sessions without it, played however you play. Maximum FPS keeps a change only when it is likely better: the average higher by more than the allowance for normal swings between sessions, and the 1% low (the worst moments) not lower by more. Otherwise the change goes back.
rule.noResult: Real play needs enough sessions on each side that can be compared fairly, so nothing was judged. The line above says what got in the way, and what happened to the change.

realPlay.noise: Judged against a ±{{band}}% band from this test's own sessions: an allowance for normal swings between your {{game}} sessions ({{before}} without the change, {{with}} with it).
realPlay.compared: Compared across {{with}} sessions with it on and {{before}} without: 1% low {{low}}%, average frame rate {{avg}}%, both against a ±{{band}}% band (the allowance for normal swings between sessions). {{rule}}
realPlay.comparedMaxFps: Judged for Maximum FPS. Compared across {{with}} sessions with it on and {{before}} without: average frame rate {{avg}}%, 1% low {{low}}%, both against a ±{{band}}% band (the allowance for normal swings between sessions). {{rule}}
realPlay.tooNoisyWhy: Your sessions varied too much from one to the next to tell this setting's effect apart, so Compy restored it and judged nothing.

verdict.confounded: Another change interfered — restored, can't attribute
verdict.expired: Baseline too old to judge — restored
verdict.insufficientEvidence: Not enough data to judge — restored

simVerdict.insufficientEvidence: Unknown — measure it to find out

experimentBench.startExperiment: Start experiment — apply & measure next session
experimentBench.ledgerBusy: Compy is still making another change, such as putting things back. You can start a Trial when it finishes.
experimentBench.fineprint: Applies one reversible change now, then compares your next {{game}} session. Auto-restores unless it clearly beats the noise floor.
experimentBench.noBaselineYet: No baseline yet — play one monitored gaming session first. Compy needs a real before-reading; it won't invent one.
experimentBench.baselineTooShort: This session is too short to compare a change against: {{readings}} of the {{min}} frame-rate readings Compy needs (about 10 minutes of play).
experimentBench.baselineUneven: This baseline was uneven: first half {{first}} fps, second half {{second}} fps, so this experiment's result may be less reliable.
experimentBench.baselineUntraced: Compy can't tell whether this baseline was steady: this session doesn't have enough of a frame-rate trace to check.
experimentBench.baselineRerecord: Record a new baseline: play another {{game}} session, then start.
experimentBench.baselineRerecordNoGame: Record a new baseline: play another session of this game, then start.
experimentBench.receiptBaselineUneven: This experiment's baseline was uneven: first half {{first}} fps, second half {{second}} fps, so its result may be less reliable.
experimentBench.receiptBaselineUntraced: Compy couldn't tell whether this experiment's baseline was steady: that session didn't have enough of a frame-rate trace to check.
experimentBench.receiptBaselineUnevenPlain: The baseline was uneven: first half {{first}} fps, second half {{second}} fps.
experimentBench.receiptAfterUneven: The after-session was uneven: first half {{first}} fps, second half {{second}} fps.
experimentBench.tooNoisyWhy: A session this uneven on its own can't tell this setting's effect apart from the scene, so Compy restored it and judged nothing.
experimentBench.receiptCompared: Compared with the baseline: 1% low {{low}}%, average frame rate {{avg}}%, both against a ±{{band}}% band. {{rule}}
experimentBench.receiptRuleKept: The 1% low rose by more than the band and the average didn't fall by more, so the change was kept.
experimentBench.receiptRulePutBack: The 1% low rose by more than the band and the average didn't fall by more, but the change was put back before Compy kept it.
experimentBench.receiptRuleAvgFell: The 1% low rose by more than the band, but the average fell by more than it, so this isn't a clear win: the default was kept and the change restored.
experimentBench.receiptRuleLowFell: The 1% low fell by more than the band, so the change was restored.
experimentBench.receiptRuleInside: The 1% low stayed inside the band, so the default was kept and the change restored.
experimentBench.receiptComparedMaxFps: Judged for Maximum FPS. Compared with the baseline: average frame rate {{avg}}%, 1% low {{low}}%, both against a ±{{band}}% band. {{rule}}
experimentBench.receiptRuleMaxKept: The average rose by more than the band and the 1% low didn't fall by more, so the change was kept.
experimentBench.receiptRuleMaxPutBack: The average rose by more than the band and the 1% low didn't fall by more, but the change was put back before Compy kept it.
experimentBench.receiptRuleMaxAvgFell: The average fell by more than the band, so the change was restored.
experimentBench.receiptRuleMaxInside: The average stayed inside the band, so the default was kept and the change restored.
experimentBench.receiptComparedSmoothest: Judged for Smoothest. Compared with the baseline: the gap between the slowest 1% of frames and a typical frame {{pacing}}% against a ±{{pacingBand}}% band, 1% low {{low}}% against a ±{{band}}% band. {{rule}}
experimentBench.receiptComparedSmoothestUnknown: Judged for Smoothest. Compared with the baseline: frame pacing couldn't be compared, 1% low {{low}}% against a ±{{band}}% band. {{rule}}
experimentBench.receiptRuleSmoothKept: Frames got steadier by more than the band and the 1% low didn't fall by more than its band, so the change was kept.
experimentBench.receiptRuleSmoothUneven: Frames got more uneven by more than the band, so the change was restored.
experimentBench.receiptRuleSmoothInside: Frame pacing stayed inside the band, so the default was kept and the change restored.
experimentBench.receiptRuleSmoothUnknown: Without frame pacing from both sessions Compy can't tell whether frames got steadier, so the default was kept and the change restored.

smoothestHeld.unmeasured: Smoothest needs at least {{sessions}} sessions of this game with nothing changed between them, each with frame pacing recorded by this version of Compy, so it knows how much the pacing varies on its own. Play this game a few more times, then pick Smoothest.
smoothestHeld.noStartPacing: Smoothest needs frame pacing from the session this Trial starts from, and that session didn't record it. Play this game once more, then start from that session.
smoothestHeld.historyUnread: Smoothest needs Compy's change history to tell which sessions ran with nothing changed, and it couldn't be read just now. Try again in a moment; if it keeps happening, check Test → Applied & history.
smoothestHeld.unknown: Compy couldn't check whether this game's frame pacing is measured yet, so Smoothest isn't offered right now.

outcomeWhy.recommended: Keeps the change only if the 1% low rises beyond the noise band and the average frame rate doesn't fall beyond it.
outcomeWhy.maxFps: Keeps the change only if the average frame rate rises beyond the noise band and the 1% low doesn't fall beyond it.
outcomeWhy.smoothest: Keeps the change only if frames get steadier beyond this game's own pacing band and the 1% low doesn't fall beyond its band.

outcomeChoice.label: Two results that disagree

reason.lowFlat: 1% lows didn't rise beyond the noise ({{pct}}%)
reason.avgFlat: average didn't rise beyond the noise ({{pct}}%)

outcomeChoice.cantTell: Compy can't read whether this change is on now, so it doesn't offer to switch.
outcomeChoice.keepStale: The result that kept {{change}} under {{outcome}} came from a different graphics card, driver or Windows build. Test it again before Compy applies it on that basis.
outcomeChoice.keepUnverified: The result that kept {{change}} under {{outcome}} can't be tied to this PC as it is now (no graphics driver or Windows build was recorded). Test it again before Compy applies it on that basis.
outcomeChoice.notFound: Compy couldn't confirm {{change}} is applied now, so nothing was undone. Check it in Test → Applied & history.
outcomeChoice.busy: Finish or stop the Trial in progress before switching.

experimentBench.pairChanged: What differed: {{changed}} changed between the before and after sessions.
experimentBench.pairUnrecorded: What differed: one of the sessions didn't record {{unrecorded}}.
experimentBench.pairBoth: What differed: {{changed}} changed, and one of the sessions didn't record {{unrecorded}}.
experimentBench.stretchLeftOut: {{session}}: {{minutes}} min with the game in the background was left out of the numbers.
experimentBench.stretchFlat: {{session}}: {{minutes}} min held at about {{fps}} fps. That may be a menu, a frame cap or the game in the background; Compy can't tell, so it was counted.
experimentBench.stretchFlatFocused: {{session}}: {{minutes}} min held at about {{fps}} fps. That may be a menu or a frame cap; Compy can't tell, so it was counted.
experimentBench.stretchCappedBoth: Both sessions held at about {{fps}} fps ({{before}} min before, {{after}} min after), which looks like one frame cap. While it holds, a change can't show a gain, so this "No measurable change" says little about the change itself.
experimentBench.receiptTooFewLeftOut: Only {{readings}} readings while the game was in front: {{span}} were left out because another window was in front.
experimentBench.baselineTooShortLeftOut: Those readings are only the time the game was in front: {{span}} were left out because another window was in front.
experimentBench.runningStep: The change is applied. Play a {{game}} session, then conclude — Compy compares it to the baseline and restores the change unless it clearly wins.
experimentBench.runningChangeOff: Compy reads {{change}} as off now, so a {{game}} session can't count toward this test. Restore now ends it and leaves the setting as it was before the test.
experimentBench.runningLegacy: An older version of Compy started this experiment and didn’t record everything a fair comparison needs, so it can’t be concluded. Restore it, then start a new one.
experimentBench.runningNoTreatment: Play a monitored {{game}} session to give the experiment a real after-reading.
experimentBench.noiseBetweenSessions: Judged against a ±{{band}}% noise floor: across {{sessions}} of your unchanged {{game}} sessions on this PC, the 1% low frame rate differed by up to {{measured}}% between sessions played with nothing changed in between. Sessions on either side of a change are never compared.
experimentBench.noiseBetweenSessionsBelowFloor: Judged against Compy's {{band}}% minimum noise floor: across {{sessions}} of your unchanged {{game}} sessions on this PC, the 1% low frame rate differed by up to {{measured}}% between sessions played with nothing changed in between, which is less than that minimum. Sessions on either side of a change are never compared.
experimentBench.noiseUnmeasured: Judged against Compy's {{band}}% noise floor. This game's own run-to-run noise on your PC hasn't been measured yet.
experimentBench.noiseMeasured: Judged against Compy's fixed {{band}}% noise floor. In one 25-second calibration on your PC, this game's 1% low varied by ±{{measured}}%. That number isn't used to judge yet, and the game version isn't checked.
experimentBench.noiseStaleChanged: Judged against Compy's {{band}}% noise floor. This game's spread on your PC was measured before a driver or Windows update, so it wasn't used. The game version isn't checked.
experimentBench.noiseStaleUnconfirmed: Judged against Compy's {{band}}% noise floor. This game's spread on your PC was measured, but Compy couldn't confirm nothing changed since, so it wasn't used. The game version isn't checked.
experimentBench.noiseNotRecorded_one: No noise-floor record was kept for this result.
experimentBench.noiseNotRecorded_other: No noise-floor record was kept for these results.
experimentBench.noiseNothingJudged_one: One result was not judged against a noise floor: its sessions could not be compared fairly.
experimentBench.noiseNothingJudged_other: {{count}} results were not judged against a noise floor: their sessions could not be compared fairly.

rule.fasterButLessSteady: the average rose beyond the band and the 1% low fell beyond it.
rule.lessSteadyNotSlower: the 1% low fell beyond the band and the average stayed within it.
